subsection.name: Introduction
subsection.p: This plugin enables centralized management of all modules to do SEO (Search Engine Optimizations) sitemap, friendly URLs, canonical URLs, robots.txt, ...

subsection.name: Friendly URLs
subsection.p: The friendly URLs module lets you create nicer URL for any resource of your site.
can be accessible with a much more friendly URL

subsection.name: Sitemap
subsection.p: The Sitemap module lets you create and generate a Sitemap file that contains all the page of your site to do a better search indexing.

subsection.name: Robots.txt
subsection.p: The robot.txt module lets you manage the file that will indicate to bots how to navigate in your site

subsection.name: URL rewriting
subsection.p: The URL rewriting module lets you create rules to redirect automatically URL to another.

subsection.name: URL rewriting diagnostic page
subsection.p: UrlRewriteFilter ships a diagnostic page displaying the rewrite rules actually loaded in memory, their parsing errors and the current request info. It tells whether a rule generated by the plugin has really been read by the filter, which neither the database nor the generated file can tell.

It is disabled by default. To enable it on a development environment, set the statusEnabled parameter of the seo_urlrewriter filter to true in WEB-INF/plugins/seo.xml ; the page is then served on <context-path>/status (value of statusPath).
Do not leave it enabled in production : access is filtered on the Host header (statusEnabledOnHosts), not on the client address.

subsection.name: Sitemap — output file
subsection.p: The sitemap is written to <webapp>/sitemap-seo.xml, a path configurable through the seo.sitemapFilePath property of WEB-INF/conf/plugins/seo.properties.

It used to be <webapp>/sitemap.xml, a path this plugin does not own. The sitemap plugin writes there as well, in hard code and with a different content — the site pages and documents, where this module publishes the friendly URLs flagged for the sitemap — so both daemons overwrote each other and the last one executed won. A site build shipping its own sitemap.xml overwrote both at every deployment.

On an existing site nothing breaks, but the Sitemap directive of robots.txt keeps pointing at the former file, which nothing updates any more : point it at the new one, then remove the obsolete sitemap.xml. As long as that file is present, every generation logs a reminder. robots.txt accepts several Sitemap directives, so the sitemap plugin can keep announcing its own. Setting the property back to /sitemap.xml restores the former behaviour.
